source.title: Theoretical Understanding of Batch-normalization: A Markov Chain Perspective
source.authors: Hadi Daneshmand; J. Kohler; F. Bach; T. Hofmann; Aurélien Lucchi

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendix; no cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures hidden-representation rank and training accuracy across depth, normalization and initialization conditions. These experiments bear on training behavior, but use a different experimental setup from the benchmark recipes in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the paper's own training-accuracy comparisons and initialization interventions. Rank-only measurements, cited findings, and pretraining comparisons that do not test a listed version are not included. Figure values are not numerically legible in the supplied text, so values are recorded as figure only.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares training accuracy with and without BN in a new setting: Fashion-MNIST ReLU MLPs. Its CIFAR-10 convolutional-network experiments also bear on training fit under different random initializations, although their short duration limits conclusions about eventual convergence.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors prove a conditional rank-preservation result for randomly initialized linear BN networks, observe related behavior in ReLU networks, and use initialization interventions and rank-increasing pretraining to argue that initial representation rank strongly influences subsequent optimization. Their theory does not prove general convergence of modern nonlinear architectures.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies rank preservation and training accuracy under BN, depth and initialization changes; it does not reproduce the listed benchmark training recipes for the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth and initialization symmetry affect training behavior. In the reported BN VGG19 comparison, omitting mean deduction is described as not affecting performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing BN centering leaves VGG19 training performance essentially unchanged.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BN's centering operation is unnecessary for comparable training performance in this tested VGG19 setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing initialization symmetry while preserving variance slows learning and reduces rank in batch-normalized VGG19 and ResNet50.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BN's optimization performance depends on initialization symmetry and representation rank, beyond initialization variance alone.

record.problems: The training-accuracy comparisons central to the extracted results are presented in figures without numerical values in the supplied text. The depth result is on Fashion-MNIST MLPs and does not directly establish the listed CIFAR/ImageNet recipe claims.
record.rows_left_out: Rank measurements in Figures 1-9 and 13 are not separate rows because they measure rank rather than training behavior named by the tested versions. The pretraining comparisons in Figures 4, 6, 11 and 12 compare a new rank-increasing procedure with BN rather than testing the listed versions' BN-versus-plain or initialization claims. Figure 10's gradient-alignment and random-data comparisons do not measure the outcomes named in these versions.

untested.parts: Eventual convergence with sufficient training; CIFAR-100; corrupted or random labels; capacity thresholds; and controlled comparisons of early stopping or regularization. Random input images in Figure 10 are not random labels.
All parts: no two-layer ReLU teacher-student minima or extra-neuron experiment.
All specified comparisons: depth degradation in batch-normalized convolutional networks, identity shortcuts, longer training, special tanh initialization, and Fixup.

Activation-matched initialization comparisons, measured prevention of exploding or vanishing signals and gradients, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and the specified very-deep plain-network experiments. The initialization-symmetry intervention addresses a related initialization mechanism.
All parts: no initial stability threshold, catapult trajectory, sharpness threshold tracking, or relevant divergence sweep.
Higher learning-rate tolerance and Fixup's normalization-free residual-network comparison.

missing.what: Record the ordinary VGG19 BN-SGD versus unnormalized SGD training-accuracy comparison. The declared exclusions cover Figure 10's gradient-alignment and random-input comparisons, but overlook this direct normalization comparison. Keep the 100× learning-rate condition separate; it does not establish a stability threshold.
missing.locator: Appendix H, Figure 10, left panel and accompanying discussion

record.verdict_notes: Exact curve values cannot be recovered from the supplied textual figure renderings. Qualitative states rely on explicit author statements. The CIFAR-10 fitting failures concern short displayed runs and do not establish bad local minima or failure after sufficiently long training. This study is not among the supplied original sources.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100 training error to zero or near zero, corrupted or random labels, model size comparisons, or early stopping and regularization effects.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or comparison of student and teacher widths.

The depth comparison is on ReLU MLPs using Fashion-MNIST, not plain batch-normalized convolutional networks on ImageNet or CIFAR-10. It does not test identity residual shortcuts against plain networks, or special initializations for plain tanh networks and residual networks without normalization.

The paper varies initialization symmetry and centering in batch-normalized VGG19 and ResNet50 experiments. It does not test activation-matched initializations, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, very deep tanh networks, or 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
No learning-rate stability threshold, catapult phase, sharpness tracking or divergence sweep.

The depth comparison is on Fashion-MNIST ReLU MLPs and does not report higher learning-rate tolerance. The paper does not test Fixup or compare residual networks trained with and without normalization.

rows.subject: ReLU multilayer perceptrons (MLPs)
rows.operation_detail: Compared training accuracy across numbers of hidden layers, with and without batch normalization.
rows.uncertainty: Mean and 95% confidence interval of 5 independent runs
rows.note: The text says vanilla networks are essentially unable to learn in a limited number of epochs above 10 layers, while BN networks' training accuracy drops only very mildly through depth 32. Exact values are figure only.
rows.check: The reported BN advantage is clear, rather than partial: after 75 epochs, unnormalized networks essentially fail to learn above 10 layers while BN networks degrade only mildly through depth 32. Remove V3: these are MLPs, and normalization replaces the claimed identity-shortcut comparison.

rows.subject: VGG19
rows.operation_detail: Trained with batch normalization under standard PyTorch initialization.
rows.uncertainty: Average and 95% CI of 5 independent runs
rows.note: The figure compares BN initialization conditions; no numeric accuracy is stated in text.
rows.check: Training accuracy on CIFAR-10 bears on V1, but the supplied figure text does not establish zero or near-zero error. This condition alone establishes neither a BN speed advantage nor V4's activation-matched initialization effect.

rows.subject: VGG19
rows.operation_detail: Trained with batch normalization after changing initialization to a nonnegative uniform distribution of the same variance.
rows.uncertainty: Average and 95% CI of 5 independent runs
rows.note: The text says this initialization reduces BN's rank-preserving quality significantly and yields much slower learning; it says VGG and ResNet cannot fit CIFAR-10 after this initialization change.
rows.check: The authors explicitly report failure to fit CIFAR-10 under nonnegative initialization within the displayed experiment, approximately eight epochs. This is a training-budget-specific failure, not evidence of eventual nonconvergence. No unnormalized comparator establishes a V6 effect, and the intervention tests initialization symmetry rather than V4's activation-matched signal/gradient scaling.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.operation_detail: Trained with batch normalization after changing initialization to a nonnegative uniform distribution of the same variance.
rows.uncertainty: Average and 95% CI of 5 independent runs
rows.note: The text says modern architectures including ResNet are unable to fit CIFAR-10 after the initialization change; exact values are figure only.
rows.check: The authors report failure to fit CIFAR-10 after the initialization change within the displayed run, approximately seven epochs. Remove V4 and V6: this is a residual network with BN in both initialization conditions, without the comparisons those versions specify.
